Extracting contrast estimates from masks and atlases

Source: vignettes/beta-extraction.Rmd
beta-extraction.Rmd

After a whole-brain fit, you might want one value per participant to plot the magnitude and direction of an effect within a region. This guide uses the completed FSL analysis from whole-brain group maps. It covers an independent atlas, clusters from AFNI, and voxel sets from pTFCE. For the latter two, first run the corresponding method in the FWE correction guide.

extract_glm_betas_in_mask() extracts FSL FEAT images. A COPE is the estimated contrast of regression coefficients. In the example, it is the face coefficient minus the house coefficient. zstat and tstat quantify evidence against the null, while varcope is the estimated within-image variance of the contrast at each voxel. The mean of a z-map is a descriptive summary. Likewise, the mean of the voxelwise VARCOPEs is generally different from the sampling variance of a regional mean.

For AFNI and SPM fits, use the image-based extraction example with the fitted coefficient or contrast images.

Choose the maps to summarize

Question FEAT level to extract Result
How did the estimated contrast differ across runs? L1 A value per participant, visit, run, contrast, and ROI
What is each participant’s combined effect? L2 in the two-run example A value per participant, visit, contrast, and ROI
What is the fitted sample effect in the ROI? L3 A value per group map and ROI

In a single-run FSL analysis, use L1 for the participant effects. L3 contains group effects, so there is no subject ID on those rows. The L3 session identifies the fitted session or is 0 for a pooled fit.

Work with the completed batch cache as described in run and reload the analysis. The extraction function reads the completed FEAT setup tables. Refresh the levels you plan to use if your snapshot predates estimation.

library(fmri.pipeline)
library(dplyr)

gpa <- refresh_glm_status(gpa, level = 2L, glm_software = "fsl")
feat <- lookup_feat_outputs(gpa, level = 2L, what = "cope", source = "setup")
subject_maps <- feat$l2 |>
  filter(
    l1_model == "facehouse", l1_cope_name == "faces_minus_houses",
    l2_model == "run_average", l2_cope_name == "EV_Intercept", session == 1L
  )

subject_maps |>
  count(analysis_status, is_passthrough, image_exists)

Compare this inventory with the participant roster and the inputs of the specific group fit. Missing files are reported and omitted during extraction. For a one-run L2 passthrough, the only available logical L2 image is the L1 COPE. Inspect the participant and session counts before analyzing the table.

Prepare the mask

A mask is a 3D NIfTI already aligned to every statistic image being summarized. The extractor checks dimensions, voxel sizes, spatial units, and voxel-to-world transforms. Verify both the template space and the image grid. If a mask comes from a different grid in the same space, resample it onto a representative COPE grid with nearest-neighbor interpolation for discrete labels. If the spaces differ, apply the appropriate spatial transform first. Overlay the result on representative COPEs and inspect coverage.

  • A binary mask uses 0 for background and 1 for one ROI.
  • An integer atlas or cluster mask uses 0 for background and a distinct integer per parcel or cluster. Keep a lookup table from label to region name.
  • A continuous mask returns voxel rows with the continuous values in mask_value. It does not automatically calculate weighted means.
  • With a 4D input, the function uses only the first volume. Supply explicit 3D masks when using a multi-volume atlas.

For atlas extraction, start with an atlas in the appropriate template space. Use distinct mask basenames if extracting several atlases into one output directory. The basename is used in the table and output filename.

Use a cluster map after AFNI correction

The AFNI correction example creates cobj, an afni_3dclusterize object. Each surviving cluster has a different integer label in cluster_map. Use cluster_table to identify the cluster IDs and their locations.

cluster_files <- cobj$get_outputs()
cobj$get_clust_df()
mask_file <- cluster_files$cluster_map

If no clusters survive, there may be no usable label map. Record the null result and skip cluster-based extraction. For descriptive exploration of large surviving clusters, generate_subclusters() raises the statistic threshold within the parent cluster and searches for smaller connected components. Alternatively, subset_atlas_against_clusters() can keep parcels that overlap the cluster mask. In the example below, each retained parcel must have at least 70% of its voxels inside the cluster mask. The default mask_by_overlap = FALSE preserves the full retained parcels.

cobj$generate_subclusters(break_nvox = 800, min_subclust_nvox = 100)
cobj$get_outputs()$subcluster_files

cobj$subset_atlas_against_clusters(
  atlas_file = "/study/atlases/aligned_parcels.nii.gz",
  minimum_overlap = 0.70, mask_by_overlap = FALSE
)
cobj$get_outputs()$atlas_files

Report any data-driven refinement along with the initial selection rule. These summaries inherit the selection of the parent corrected map.

Use surviving voxels after pTFCE

The pTFCE result manifest gives you a thresholded, signed statistic image. Convert it to integer labels to summarize by direction. The example makes one ROI for all surviving positive voxels and another for all surviving negative voxels, including disconnected components. The output image inherits geometry from the statistic image. The underlying values for extraction still come from the unthresholded COPEs.

ptfce_image <- fwe_result_artifacts(
  fwe_result,
  artifact_role = "thresholded_statistic",
  l3_cope_name = "EV_Intercept", fwe_alpha = 0.05
)
stopifnot(nrow(ptfce_image) == 1L, ptfce_image$can_use_as_mask)

signed_stat <- RNifti::readNifti(ptfce_image$artifact_file)
labels <- signed_stat
labels[] <- 0L
labels[signed_stat > 0] <- 1L
labels[signed_stat < 0] <- 2L
table(as.integer(labels))

if (!any(labels != 0L)) {
  stop("No voxels survived at the selected alpha.")
}

mask_file <- file.path(gpa$output_directory, "faces_minus_houses_ptfce_05_signs.nii.gz")
RNifti::writeNifti(labels, mask_file, datatype = "int16")

Extract and check the table

For an independent atlas, set mask_file to your aligned integer atlas instead. If needed, obtain that file by resampling a pre-specified atlas to the grid of one of the L2 COPEs as described above.

mask_file <- "/study/atlases/aligned_parcels.nii.gz"

Run the following at an interactive R console. For this L2 call, choose facehouse when prompted for the contributing L1 model. For L3 extraction, the prompts also ask for lower-level models. The extract_l1, extract_l2, and extract_l3 arguments each take one name, "all", "prompt", or "none". Selecting "all" at a higher level still asks about its inputs.

roi <- extract_glm_betas_in_mask(
  gpa,
  mask_files = mask_file,
  what = "cope",
  extract_l1 = "none",
  extract_l2 = "run_average",
  extract_l3 = "none",
  aggregate = TRUE,
  scheduler = "local",
  out_dir = file.path(gpa$output_directory, "roi_effects")
)

stopifnot(NROW(roi$l2) > 0L)
effect <- roi$l2 |>
  filter(
    l1_cope_name == "faces_minus_houses", l2_cope_name == "EV_Intercept",
    session == 1L
  ) |>
  select(id, session, mask_name, mask_value, value)

effect |>
  group_by(mask_name, mask_value) |>
  summarize(
    n_participants = n_distinct(id),
    n_finite = sum(is.finite(value)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

The function returns a list with l1, l2, and l3 elements. By default it also writes CSVs grouped by L1 model, mask basename, statistic, and level. The L2 example writes roi_effects/L1m-facehouse/<mask_name>_cope_l2.csv.gz. Keep the contrast and session columns when joining output tables that contain several fits. With write_data = FALSE, only the returned object is produced.

For integer masks, aggregate = TRUE returns one summary per label and image, using mean unless you set aggFUN. Near-zero statistic values are treated as missing by the extractor to account for voxels outside a fit’s coverage. An ROI with no usable voxels can have a non-finite summary, and coverage can vary across participants. The returned x, y, and z are the label’s centroid in NIfTI world coordinates for aggregated rows. With aggregate = FALSE, the table includes voxel values, one-based indices i, j, k, and world coordinates for each voxel. Start with a small selection because a voxelwise table can grow quickly.

A plot can show the participant values that went into a regional summary.

ggplot2::ggplot(effect, ggplot2::aes(x = factor(mask_value), y = value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey65") +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "ROI label", y = "Faces minus houses COPE")

If the ROI was selected using the same group contrast and participants, use this plot descriptively. The selected effect sizes can be inflated and an ordinary second test of the same effect within the selected region does not supply independent confirmation. For confirmatory ROI inference, define regions independently of the tested data, for example using an a priori atlas, an independent localizer, or held-out participants. A different contrast from the same data is independent only under an appropriate design and null hypothesis. Kriegeskorte et al. (2009)

Extract directly from AFNI or SPM images

In a native AFNI or SPM analysis, the L1 fit supplies one contrast image per participant and visit by default. The engine guide shows where to find each fit. Read contrasts.tsv from an AFNI L1 directory or spm_contrasts.tsv from an SPM L1 directory. Both identify the effect image in coef_file. Select the intended contrast by name and use the fit’s coverage mask to restrict the summary. The following example takes a mean per parcel from one fit.

fit_dir <- "/study/analysis/afni_l1/sub-01/facehouse"
manifest <- read.delim(file.path(fit_dir, "contrasts.tsv"))
coef_file <- manifest$coef_file[manifest$contrast_name == "faces_minus_houses"]
stopifnot(length(coef_file) == 1L, file.exists(coef_file))

estimate <- RNifti::readNifti(coef_file)
atlas <- RNifti::readNifti("/study/atlases/aligned_parcels.nii.gz")
coverage <- RNifti::readNifti(file.path(fit_dir, "mask.nii.gz"))

same_grid <- function(img) {
  identical(dim(img), dim(atlas)) &&
    isTRUE(all.equal(
      RNifti::xform(img, useQuaternionFirst = FALSE),
      RNifti::xform(atlas, useQuaternionFirst = FALSE)
    ))
}
stopifnot(same_grid(estimate), same_grid(coverage))

keep <- atlas > 0 & coverage != 0 & is.finite(estimate)
tapply(estimate[keep], as.integer(atlas[keep]), mean)

For SPM, use the SPM fit directory, its manifest, and its model mask (typically mask.nii). Verify the template and voxel units as in mask preparation. Repeat for each fit and keep the participant, session, model, and contrast with each set of parcel values.
